newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, EIB in talks on flood damage loan.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, EIB in talks on flood damage loan.

text.p: The Czech government has begun discussions with the European Investment Bank (EIB) on a loan of more than 10 billion crowns to help finance reconstruction of infrastructure damaged in recent floods, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip told reporters on Thursday.

"Such a loan would be under conditions incomparable with those under which the state is raising money in standard operations. I am not able to estimate the sum..." Pilip said. "But it is clear that when talking about reconstruction of infrastructure, it would not be a sum in the range of 10 billion (crowns) but something certainly higher," he said.

Parts of the eastern third of the country were inundated last week as rivers swelled to their highest levels this century after torrential rains. More than 40 people have been reported killed in the floods.
The flooding shut dozens of major road and rail links and forced many factories to close, partly because they could not move their output to customers.
Pilip put the damage to major roads and highways alone at over four billion crowns.
"We offered the Czech government a global loan for the refurbishment of damaged roads and public utilities," EIB vice president Wolfgang Roth told reporters alogside Pilip.
The EIB is the long-term financing arm of the European Union, focusing on regional development, providing credit also to countries associated with the EU.
Pilip and Roth on Thursday signed an already agreed 200 million ECU loan from the EIB to help finance a high-speed rail corridor cutting through the Czech Republic.
